source.title: Sparse maximal update parameterization: A holistic approach to sparse training dynamics
source.authors: Nolan Dey; Shane Bergsma; Joel Hestness

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that sparse training outcomes and optimal hyperparameters depend on sparsity and parameterization; it does not test the listed classification-error, local-minimum, depth, initialization, learning-rate-stability, or batch-normalization versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study trains sparse transformer language models and reports training or validation loss under different parameterizations and sparsity levels. It does not report CIFAR classification training error. Prior-work results mentioned in the paper are not recorded as rows. Values used only to choose optimal hyperparameters are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures sparse transformer losses, activation scales, and hyperparameter transfer. These results do not test any listed version. In particular, sparsity-aware initialization and hyperparameter transfer do not measure V4's faster learning or greater trainable depth in plain networks, and learning-rate sweeps without curvature or stability thresholds do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate when restricted to random unstructured static sparsity. The authors conclude that increasing sparsity under SP and µP causes vanishing activations and hyperparameter detuning, while SµPar jointly controls initialization and updates, enables hyperparameter transfer, and improves language-model loss. They explicitly require further extension for dynamic and nonrandom sparsity.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates SµPar, a sparsity-aware parameterization, on GPT-like language models using SlimPajama. It does not reproduce the listed classification-error studies or their recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes and optimal hyperparameters vary with sparsity level and parameterization. For dynamic sparse methods, the authors report that no tested parameterization provides stable optimal learning-rate transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: At 99.2% random static sparsity, SµPar achieves 11.9% lower validation loss than SP and 1.9% lower than µP. The authors attribute much of the gap to detuned comparator learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint sparsity-aware initialization and learning-rate scaling improve sparse transformer loss when transferring dense hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: SµPar preserves approximately optimal learning rates across tested static sparsity levels and Iso-Parameter scaling, whereas SP and µP optima shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SµPar enables hyperparameter transfer across width and random static sparsity in the tested transformer models.

fits_no_version.finding: For RigL and GMP, none of the three parameterizations preserves optimal learning rates across sparsity; SµPar overcorrects, and some sweep runs diverge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested static-sparsity parameterizations do not ensure learning-rate transfer for RigL or GMP.

record.problems: The listed training-loss and validation-loss results are largely presented in figures without transcribed numeric values. The experiments are language modeling on SlimPajama, so they do not directly establish the listed classification-error claims. Dynamic-sparsity learning-rate transfer is reported as unstable, with some runs diverging.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for Figures 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, or 14: those results focus on optimal initialization or learning-rate selection, or summarize/repeat the same training-loss comparisons, rather than separately reporting a claim-version outcome. Downstream-task accuracy in Table 2 is not training classification error.

untested.parts: All: CIFAR convolutional-network training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and size, stopping, or regularization comparisons.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequency, and extra student neurons.
All: depth degradation in plain convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated initialization exceptions.
All: activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh and convolutional comparisons.
All: learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery with curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from below the threshold.
All: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 classification contradicts its own version assessments. The initialization-only ablations concern hyperparameter transfer, not a demonstrated failure of V4's learning-speed or trainable-depth claims. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not dispute the reported sparse-training findings.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses language modeling and reports loss, not CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted labels, random labels, or the stated model-size and stopping comparisons.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum frequency, or student-width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison, ImageNet or CIFAR-10 classification training error, or shortcut ablation.
The study adjusts initialization for width and sparsity in transformer language models, but does not test the stated activation-matched initialization, depth, tanh, or orthogonal-weight claims.
The study sweeps learning rates but does not test learning rates relative to a stability threshold, curvature changes, or the catapult and edge-of-stability behaviors.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: 610M parameter models; SµPar
rows.size_stated: 610M parameters; hidden size 2048, 10 layers, attention head size 64
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation loss across random unstructured static sparsity levels using SµPar.
rows.note: The text says SµPar forms the Pareto frontier for loss across sparsity levels; the figure provides the plotted values.
rows.check: Comparison of the study's method with other parameterizations, outside all versions. The value need not remain figure-only: the text reports 11.9% lower validation loss than SP and 1.9% lower than µP at 99.2% sparsity. The 610M size describes the starting dense configuration; sparsification reduces nonzero parameters.

rows.subject: GPT-like transformer language models; SµPar
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across sparsity levels and learning-rate sweeps.
rows.note: Authors state the SµPar optimal learning rate is consistently near 2−6 across sparsity levels. The study's result concerns loss and hyperparameter transfer, not classification error.
rows.check: Learning-rate selection sweep for the proposed method, rather than a listed claim outcome. Stable optimal learning rates across sparsity do not establish a stability threshold or recovery above it.
